about: E6 perceptual lip-sync stimuli (docs/eval/evaluation-plan.md, E6). Ten caregiver sentences taken verbatim from the shipped knowledge base (apps/mobile/src/features/library/data/knowledgeBase.js), plus one control sentence. Selection rule: 12-18 words (about 5-9 s at the app's default speech rate 0.78), no digits, abbreviations or brackets, neutral or warm in tone (raters are colleagues, not carers), and between them every visible articulation class: lip closures (p b m), lip-teeth contact (f v), tongue-teeth (th), rounded and open vowels. The control sentence is not in the main set, so it adds no repeat exposure.

main.text: Use a calm, slow voice and get to the person's eye level.
Avoid long daytime naps, which reduce the drive to sleep at night.
Brightly coloured plates that contrast with the food help the person see and identify what they are eating.
Maintain at least one activity each week that is purely for your own enjoyment.
Hearing a familiar, calm voice provides comfort regardless of whether the language is fully comprehended.
Phone calls, video calls, and brief visits sustain the relationships that provide emotional resilience.
Shared responsibility is more sustainable than one person carrying the full burden.
Personalise the bedroom door with a meaningful photograph or familiar object so the person can identify their room.
Mirror the person's body language subtly to create a sense of connection and ease.
If someone does a task differently than you would, resist correcting unless it is genuinely unsafe.

control.text: A predictable, structured daily routine is one of the most effective tools in dementia care.
